title: Radiation and dual checkpoint blockade activate non-redundant immune mechanisms in cancer

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Radiation and dual checkpoint blockade activate non-redundant immune mechanisms in cancer》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-1】Immune checkpoint inhibitors result in impressive clinical responses, but optimal results will require combination with each other and other therapies.

evidence.text: Immune checkpoint inhibitors result in impressive clinical responses, but optimal results will require combination with each other and other therapies.

sections.title: 研究方法
sections.text:
《Radiation and dual checkpoint blockade activate non-redundant immune mechanisms in cancer》：方法与研究设计的原文依据。

【Abstract · abstract-1-3】Here we report major tumour regressions in a subset of patients with metastatic melanoma treated with an anti-CTLA4 antibody (anti-CTLA4) and radiation, and reproduced this effect in mouse models.

【Abstract · abstract-1-11】Similarly to results from mice, patients on our clinical trial with melanoma showing high PD-L1 did not respond to radiation plus anti-CTLA4, demonstrated persistent T-cell exhaustion, and rapidly progressed.

evidence.text: Here we report major tumour regressions in a subset of patients with metastatic melanoma treated with an anti-CTLA4 antibody (anti-CTLA4) and radiation, and reproduced this effect in mouse models.

Similarly to results from mice, patients on our clinical trial with melanoma showing high PD-L1 did not respond to radiation plus anti-CTLA4, demonstrated persistent T-cell exhaustion, and rapidly progressed.
